summary: James G. Mullens is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University and held a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.
James Gibbs (1825–1886) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1870–1879) and President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1876–1881).

James H. Austin (b. 1925) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nanrei Kobori, Joshu Sasaki, and Katsujo Terayama. He held posts at the universities of Oregon, Missouri, Idaho, and Colorado (~1965–1992), alongside several sabbatical posts.

James Hadley (1821–1872) was a linguist who studied at Yale College (~1840–1842) and under Edward Elbridge Salisbury (1849). He held posts at Middlebury College (1844–1845) and Yale University (1845–1872).

James Haughton Woods (1864–1935) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Harvard, Strasbourg, and under Paul Deussen, Arthur Venis, Mukunda Shastri Adkar, and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He held a post at Harvard in 1914.

James Irving Manatt (1845–1915) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. Educated at Grinnell and Yale under William Dwight Whitney, he held posts at Denison, Marietta, the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, the United States, and Brown University (~1892–1915).

James Ishmael Ford (b. 1948) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied under Houn Jiyu-Kennett and John Tarrant, attended the Pacific School of Religion (~1988–1991), and founded Boundless Way Zen.

James Kenneth Powell II is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Northwestern, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD, 1998). His teachers included David Tracy, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.

James L. Fitzgerald (b. 1948) is an Indologist. He held professorships at the University of Tennessee (attested 2004–2006) and at Brown University (attested 2019) as Das Professor of Sanskrit in the Department of Classics.

James Mallinson (b. 1970) specializes in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Eton and the University of Oxford (D.Phil. 1995–2003) under Alexis Sanderson, he became Lecturer in Sanskrit and Classical Indian Studies at SOAS in 2013.

James Mark Shields (b. 1971) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. In 2016, he was attested as Associate Professor at Bucknell University and Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.
James Matthew Baskind specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Yale University under the supervision of Stanley Weinstein (attested 2006).

James McHugh works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard (PhD), taught by scholars including Alexis Sanderson, Lawrence McCrea, Anne E. Monius, and Parimal G. Patil. He held posts at USC and Cornell.

James Miller works in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge (MA, 1997) and Boston University (PhD, 2000), later serving as Professor of Chinese Studies and Religious Studies at Queen's University Belfast (attested 2014).
James Montgomery (b. 1962) studied at the University of Glasgow (~1980–1989). In 1997, he took up a post at the Faculty of Asian and Middle Eastern Studies at Cambridge.
James Morison was an Indology scholar who studied under Georg Bühler. He served as Librarian at the University of Oxford (attested 1917–1920).

James Prinsep (1799–1840) worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He was Assistant to the Assay Master at the India Government Mint in Kolkata (1819) and a member of the Asiatic Society (1832–1838), succeeding Horace Hayman Wilson in 1833.

James R. Ballantyne (1813–1864) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Edinburgh under James Michael and Francis Johnson. He taught at the Scottish Naval and Military Academy, headed Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and was librarian at the India Office Library.
James Rennell (1742–1830) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the East India Company from 1762 to 1777 and joined the Bengal Engineers in 1764.

James Robson (b. 1965) specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts as Assistant Professor at the University of Michigan (attested 2006–2014) and Associate Professor at Harvard University (~2008).
